question:
The **packing fraction** $f$ (one common convention) is defined as

$f=\frac{M-A}{A}\times 10^4$

where $M$ is the **atomic mass** in $u$ and $A$ is the mass number.

You are given atomic masses:

- $M(^{4}\!\text{He})=4.0026032\,u$
- $M(^{56}\!\text{Fe})=55.9349421\,u$
- $M(^{238}\!\text{U})=238.0507826\,u$

(a) Compute $f$ for $^{4}\!\text{He}$, $^{56}\!\text{Fe}$ and $^{238}\!\text{U}$.

(b) Using the **sign and magnitude** of $f$, identify which nucleus is **most stable** among these.

(c) Based on the idea that systems tend to move toward **higher stability**, state whether fusion of light nuclei toward intermediate masses and/or fission of heavy nuclei toward intermediate masses can release energy.

options.A: $f(^{4}\!\text{He})\approx +6.51,\; f(^{56}\!\text{Fe})\approx -11.62,\; f(^{238}\!\text{U})\approx +2.13$; $^{56}\!\text{Fe}$ is most stable, so **fusion** of light nuclei and **fission** of heavy nuclei can release energy by moving toward intermediate-mass nuclei
options.B: $f(^{4}\!\text{He})\approx +6.51,\; f(^{56}\!\text{Fe})\approx -11.62,\; f(^{238}\!\text{U})\approx +2.13$; $^{4}\!\text{He}$ is most stable, so only **fission** of light nuclei can release energy
options.C: $f(^{4}\!\text{He})\approx -6.51,\; f(^{56}\!\text{Fe})\approx +11.62,\; f(^{238}\!\text{U})\approx -2.13$; $^{238}\!\text{U}$ is most stable, so only **fusion** of heavy nuclei can release energy
options.D: $f(^{4}\!\text{He})\approx +0.651,\; f(^{56}\!\text{Fe})\approx -1.162,\; f(^{238}\!\text{U})\approx +0.213$; packing fraction is too small to indicate stability, so no conclusion about fusion/fission can be made
